correctness.rationale: For every integer n≥3, the total-momentum decomposition diagonalizes the symmetric free hopping. Apart from n-even alternating total momentum, each energy in a fixed sector is simple modulo bosonic exchange. Edge amplitude vanishes precisely for momentum-antipodal pairs, each with zero energy. The alternating sector is entirely at energy zero and the observed edge subspace has rank one. Counting these orthogonal modes proves dimension 0 for odd n, n−1 for n divisible by four, n−2 for n≡2 mod four. The exact normalized Fourier projector gives every initial-distance absorption probability. Finite-dimensional contraction excludes additional nondecaying generalized modes and yields arbitrary-positive-rate capture 1−Tr(P_D rho). Standalone modular-observability ranks for n=3…16 over two primes and a numerically separate spectral projector for n=3…14 reproduce all stated formulas; these finite tests support, not replace, the all-n proof.

value.rationale: Adjacent-site two-body annihilation is a directly motivated distance-selective lattice-boson loss mechanism in arXiv:1207.6291. The all-n theorem completely classifies when finite-strength annihilation admits indefinitely protected two-particle states, exhibits a mathematically sharp odd/even and mod-four boundary, and provides exact and experimentally interpretable distance-resolved capture probabilities robust to every positive nonuniform edge rate. The result distinguishes a true decoherence-free subspace from long-lived Zeno transients and is not an arbitrary finite calculation, parameter renaming or a marginal improvement. It does not claim larger-system thermodynamic conclusions.
